name: Invisible text instruction
description: Instructions hidden using CSS to make text invisible to humans but readable by agents. The hiding styles display none, visibility hidden and white text on a white background are flagged where they appear in the forms the tests cover, with one structural tag-name exception: a start tag whose name, spelled in ASCII letters, is an image, input, meta, source, track, embed, line break or rule tag, or a frame or a script tag closed at once, followed by whitespace, a slash or the end of the tag. Tags of that kind hold no text of their own in an HTML document, so an input that holds an svg or math start tag gets no exception at all, because the same names can hold text in that content. A name that only starts like one of these, or that uses a non ASCII letter that folds onto an ASCII one, is another element and is flagged, and so is a link tag. The words in the attribute text on the excepted tags are not read. The attribute text is parsed one attribute at a time, a name and then an optional equals sign and value, and a quote opens a quoted value only directly after that equals sign. A greater or less sign inside a quoted value therefore does not end the tag or stand in for a closing tag, a quoted word is not an attribute name, and a quote inside an unquoted value or a name makes the tag unparseable, so the exception is withdrawn and the element is flagged. A frame with an attribute named srcdoc is flagged however the other attributes are written, as long as the quotes, equals signs and angle brackets in the text are the ones the reader sees. Where a character reference, an escape or a full width mark writes one of them, the folded text and the original cut the tag at different places, so the exception is not granted anywhere in that text and a hidden tag of that kind is flagged. A hidden element outside the exception is flagged, including hidden interface text such as a closed cookie dialog. Tag like text inside a quoted attribute value is not a tag, so a hidden container whose attribute value holds the name of an excepted tag is still flagged, and the hiding style may sit inside a quoted value of the same tag. A second regex keeps the plain reading so that an unbalanced quote cannot hide a style from the rule.
